_about: The film's one musical cue (design/SOUND_BIBLE.md §4-5): it starts on the last blink, carries the corner, holds over CUT TO BLACK and resolves under the title MY NAME IS OREN, then decays with the fade (A54-A58). Made with Lyria 3.5 through tools/lyria.py: four takes from four wordings of the same controls, each windowed to its best 20-25 s with earshot `find`, checked with `describe`, judged in the order of score-and-sound-design.md §8, then chosen by ear. start_s/end_s are placeholders until Q22 exists; the cue is placed on Q22's own clock then. Prompts give mechanics, not composers or genres.

motifs.M: the theme: a small, warm guitar figure in A. Planted as fragments (M02's falling three notes, M04's rising phrase on her rank), heard whole only at the end (M01c), so the ending lands as recognition

cues.job: recognition and earned warmth as he matches her pace; resolve under the title
cues.prompt: Instrumental film-score cue, about 24 seconds, for the last shot of a quiet British short film: two people turn a street corner together, slowly, and the title appears on black. A single felt piano plays a short, simple, warm melodic figure, slow and rubato with no audible pulse, over a very soft sustained string bed. Start with no attack, almost out of silence. Major key with gentle suspended tones that resolve late; open intervals; very sparse, few notes, lots of space. Close and intimate at first, the register opening gently upward near the end, then a natural decay into silence. Tender, hopeful, restrained, never triumphant or sentimental. No drums, no vocals, no choir, no swells. In tune at A = 440.

cues.prompt: Instrumental film-score cue, about 24 seconds, for the final moment of an intimate British short film as two people walk around a corner at the same slow pace and the screen goes to black for the title. One solo cello plays a slow, simple, warm phrase, rubato, unhurried, over a quiet held chord on harmonium. It begins from near silence, stays low and close, then lifts gently in register as the phrase resolves on a major chord and fades away naturally. Very sparse and calm: sustained tones, few attacks, open fifths and a late resolution. Warm, tender, quietly hopeful. No drums, no vocals, no choir, no build-up. In tune at A = 440.

Gentle, tender, hopeful, understated. No drums, no vocals, no choir, no swells. In tune at A = 440.

cues.prompt: Instrumental film-score cue, about 35 seconds, for the opening of an intimate British short film: a grey, busy city street where one woman goes unnoticed. A very quiet, sustained low string drone on A, cellos and violas, almost subliminal, breathing slowly between A minor and A minor with an added ninth. After about 14 seconds a single nylon-string guitar enters with three slow, low, plucked notes, a small falling minor figure, then a long silence, then the same three notes once more, a step lower, like a memory. Free in time, no pulse. Sparse, close and dry, melancholy and tender, never sentimental. The guitar stops; the drone thins and fades to silence at the end. No drums, no percussion, no vocals, no choir, no synthesizers. In tune at A = 440.

A solo cello plays very long, soft notes low in its range, A and then C and then back to A, barely moving, over a faint sustained viola harmonic. Around the middle a nylon-string guitar plays a small, slow, falling three-note figure in A minor, pauses, and repeats it once, softer. Free in time, no beat, lots of silence between notes. Melancholy, intimate, restrained, like someone nobody sees. Fades to silence. No drums, no percussion, no vocals, no choir, no synthesizers. In tune at A = 440.

cues.prompt: Instrumental film-score cue, about 40 seconds, the turning point of an intimate short film, when someone is finally recognised. It begins almost inaudibly: quiet strings hold an open fifth on A and E. Over about fifteen seconds a soft C sharp enters in the violas, so the bare chord slowly turns warm and major. Then a nylon-string guitar plays a short, simple, rising phrase in A major, three or four slow notes, free in time, and pauses; the strings answer with one gentle swell and settle; the guitar repeats the phrase once, a little higher, unfinished. The cue thins to a single held string note and fades to silence. Moved, restrained, intimate, never grand. No drums, no percussion, no vocals, no choir, no synthesizers. In tune at A = 440.

cues.prompt: Instrumental film-score cue, about 40 seconds. A very slow, very quiet string chord on A rises from silence and warms from an open fifth to a full, soft A major over twenty seconds, like a face lifting. At its warmest a nylon-string guitar plays a slow, simple melodic phrase of a few notes, tender and plain, and the strings hold underneath; then everything gently recedes to a single held note and silence. Free in time, no pulse, intimate and restrained, deeply felt but understated. No drums, no percussion, no vocals, no choir, no synthesizers. In tune at A = 440.

Now and then a viola adds a note a semitone above that hangs, unresolved, then falls back. Grave, dignified, quietly angry, with no real melody, just weight and patience. It never swells. No drums, no percussion, no vocals, no choir, no synthesizers. In tune at A = 440.

_round1: M01a-d (felt piano / cello / guitar / piano+quartet): earshot heard all four as sad, not warm-hopeful (sad 80-97% in forced choice). Round 2 keeps the restraint and moves the levers FME-24 says matter for valence: a clear major key, a lighter mid-high register, relief.

chosen.take: audio/score/M01c.mp3 (Lyria 3.5, 62.1 s; raw take, not committed)
chosen.why: a single nylon-string guitar, slow plucked notes free in time over a barely audible string pad: the most minimal of the takes, like someone finally slowing down
chosen.placement: on Q22's own clock once it exists: entering on the last blink, carrying the corner, resolving under the title. Re-window then with earshot `find` so the take's resolving chord lands on the title (the take resolves late), and measure its tuning (Lyria drifts 0 to +36 cents; it plays alone, so only correct a drift you can hear).

_about_2: 2026-11-25, the author: the film should make you feel before it makes you understand, with music as part of one emotional language (design/EMOTIONAL_LANGUAGE.md). The score now runs through the film in one small ensemble (nylon-string guitar, strings) in A: minor and bare early, warming to A major; M01c stays the full statement at the end.
